exposure: gender of the newborn (preference for male babies)
no living children from prior pregnancies
previous bad experience with vaginal delivery
opinions of close relatives and friends
outcome: Cesarean Section on Maternal Request (CSMR) rate
factors affecting patient decisions regarding mode of delivery
cohort: The study included patients admitted for normal vaginal delivery who requested an elective cesarean section, excluding those with obstetric indications for a C-section.
finding: The overall C-section rate was found to be 36.7%, with 10% of these cases attributed to Cesarean Section on Maternal Request (CSMR).
mod_finding: Factors influencing the patient's decision for Cesarean Section on Maternal Request (CSMR) included previous C-section, newborn gender preference, prior bad vaginal delivery experience, and influence from close relatives, friends, and doctors.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from patients at the time of admission for delivery decision-making.
